subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the correct solution depends on durable storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, and migration choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle the memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Narrow to memory-core only
options.body: Limit v1 to bundled memory-core CLI and SQLite behavior, accepting that external memory plugins will need a later API alignment step.

options.title: Defer the MVP
options.body: Leave current search/promotion/dreaming behavior in place and keep concrete stale-memory bugs tracked separately until memory lifecycle work becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle the memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent storage/schema and memory SDK history makes this the best available routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
